units.literal: Gentlemen at court who manage selection and great officials, if able not because of the person to discard words, raise and put them in practice, each taking yielding to worthies and raising ability as first task, then host of talents will swarm forth, able and unable will be sharply distinguished — age-surpassing achievement, nothing greater than this.

units.zh: 泰始初，進爵為伯，累遷少府。
units.en: Early in Taishi his noble rank rose to earl, and he was promoted step by step to privy treasurer.
units.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he advanced in noble rank to earl, by accumulated transfers became Privy Treasurer.

units.zh: 咸甯中為太常。
units.en: During the Xianning era he served as minister of ceremonies.
units.literal: In Xianning he was Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 轉尚書。
units.en: He was transferred to the masters of writing.
units.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 杜預之伐吳也，寔以本官行鎮南軍司。
units.en: When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Liu Shi, still in his current post, served as army director on the southern pacification staff.
units.literal: When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Shi by his original office acted as Army Director of the Southern Pacification command.

units.zh: 初，寔妻盧氏生子躋而卒，華氏將以女妻之。
units.en: Earlier, Shi's wife of the Lu clan bore a son, Ji, then died; the Hua family wished to give him a daughter in marriage.
units.literal: Earlier, Shi's wife the Lu clan bore a son Ji and died; the Hua clan was about to take a daughter and marry her to him.

units.zh: 寔弟智諫曰：「華家類貪，必破門戶。」
units.en: His brother Zhi warned him, "The Huas are a grasping clan; they will ruin our house."
units.literal: Shi's younger brother Zhi remonstrated, saying, "The Hua clan is by kind greedy; they will surely break the household gate."

units.zh: 辭之不得，竟婚華氏而生子夏。
units.en: Shi could not refuse the match; he married a Hua daughter and fathered a son named Xia.
units.literal: Declining it he could not obtain; in the end he married the Hua clan and bore a son Xia.

units.zh: 寔竟坐夏受賂，免官。
units.en: In the end Shi lost his office because Xia took bribes.
units.literal: Shi in the end, because Xia was convicted of accepting bribes, was dismissed from office.

units.zh: 頃之為大司農，又以夏罪免。
units.en: Soon he was named grand minister of agriculture, then dismissed again over Xia's crimes.
units.literal: Before long he was Grand Minister of Agriculture, again because of Xia's crime dismissed.

units.zh: 寔每還州裏，鄉人載酒肉以候之。
units.en: Whenever Shi returned to his home district, villagers brought wine and meat to greet him.
units.literal: Whenever Shi returned to the commandery district, townsmen loaded wine and meat to await him.

units.zh: 寔難逆其意，輒共啖而返其餘。
units.en: Unwilling to refuse their kindness outright, he would share a little of the feast and send the rest back.
units.literal: Shi found it hard to go against their intent, then always together ate and returned the remainder.

units.zh: 或謂寔曰：「君行高一世，而諸子不能遵。
units.en: Someone said to him, "Your conduct towers above the age, yet your sons will not follow your example.
units.literal: Someone said to Shi, "Your conduct is high above one age, yet the various sons cannot follow.

units.zh: 何不旦夕切磋，使知過而自改邪！」
units.en: Why not lecture them day and night until they see their faults and mend their ways?"
units.literal: Why not morning and evening cut and polish, causing them to know fault and themselves reform!"

units.zh: 寔曰：「吾之所行，是所聞見，不相祖習，豈復教誨之所得乎！」
units.en: Shi answered, "What I do rests on what I myself saw and heard; my sons have not walked the same path—how could mere lecturing reach them now?"
units.literal: Shi said, "What I practice is what I heard and saw; we do not mutually imitate and practice — how again could instruction and teaching obtain it!"

units.zh: 世以寔言為當。
units.en: People of the time judged his reply sound.
units.literal: The age held Shi's words correct.

units.zh: 後起為國子祭酒、散騎常侍。
units.en: Later he was recalled as libationer of the imperial academy and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Later he rose as Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 湣懷太子初封廣陵王，高選師友，以寔為師。
units.en: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first enfeoffed as prince of Guangling, the court chose his tutors with care and named Shi his principal teacher.
units.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, highly selecting teachers and friends, they made Shi his teacher.

units.zh: 元康初，進爵為侯，累遷太子太保，加侍中、特進、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，領冀州都督。
units.en: Early in Yuankang his rank rose to marquis; he rose through junior tutor to the heir apparent to the added titles of palace attendant, specially advanced, grand master of the right of splendid carriage, and opener of a bureau with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, while commanding military affairs in Ji Province.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang he advanced in noble rank to marquis, by accumulated transfers became Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, added Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Grand Master of the Right of Splendid Carriage, Opener of Office with parity of the Three Dukes, concurrently Area Commander of Ji Province.

units.zh: 九年，策拜司空，遷太保，轉太傅。
units.en: In the ninth year of the era he received the rescript as minister of works, then moved up to grand guardian and finally grand tutor.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was rescript-appointed Minister of Works, transferred Grand Guardian, transferred Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 太安初，寔以老病遜位，賜安車駟馬、錢百萬，以侯就第。
units.en: Early in the Tai'an era he resigned on grounds of age and illness; the court granted him a secure carriage, four-horse team, a million cash, and permission to retire to his mansion as a marquis.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tai'an, Shi because of old age and illness yielded position; he was bestowed secure carriage and four-horse team, one million cash, and as marquis went to mansion.

units.zh: 及長沙成都之相攻也，寔為軍人所掠，潛歸鄉里。
units.en: When the princes of Changsha and Chengdu turned on each other, soldiers plundered him and he slipped away to his home district.
units.literal: When Changsha and Chengdu mutually attacked, Shi was plundered by soldiers and secretly returned to his home village.

units.zh: 惠帝崩，寔赴山陵。
units.en: When Emperor Hui died, Shi went to attend at the imperial mausoleum.
units.literal: Emperor Hui died; Shi went to the imperial mausoleum.

units.zh: 懷帝即位，復授太尉。
units.en: When Emperor Huai succeeded to the throne, he again appointed Shi as grand commandant.
units.literal: Emperor Huai took the throne and again appointed him Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 寔自陳年老，固辭，不許。
units.en: Shi pleaded old age and firmly declined the post, but the court would not allow it.
units.literal: Shi himself stated he was old in years, firmly declined, and was not permitted.

units.zh: 左丞劉坦上言曰：「夫堂高級遠，主尊相貴。
units.en: Left Deputy Liu Tan submitted a memorial, saying, "When the hall is high, the steps are far; when the sovereign is honored, the minister is exalted.
units.literal: Left Deputy Liu Tan submitted a memorial saying, "When the hall is high the steps are far; the lord is honored and the minister noble.

units.zh: 是以古之哲王莫不師其元臣，崇養老之教，訓示四海，使少長有禮。
units.en: For this reason the wise kings of antiquity all looked to their chief ministers as teachers, honored the instruction to nurture the aged, and taught all within the seas so that young and old alike observed proper ritual.
units.literal: Therefore the wise kings of antiquity all took their chief ministers as teachers, esteemed the teaching of nurturing the old, instructed and displayed to the four seas, making young and old have ritual.

units.zh: 七十致仕，亦所以優異舊德，厲廉高之風。
units.en: Retirement at seventy was likewise meant to honor aged virtue and sharpen the standards of integrity and lofty conduct.
units.literal: Retiring from office at seventy was also a means to specially distinguish old virtue and sharpen the wind of integrity and loftiness.

units.zh: 太尉寔體清素之操，執不渝之潔，懸車告老，二十餘年，浩然之志，老而彌篤。
units.en: Grand Commandant Shi embodies pure and simple conduct and unwavering integrity; he hung up his carriage and announced retirement more than twenty years ago, and his vast resolve has grown only firmer with age.
units.literal: Grand Commandant Shi embodies pure and simple conduct, holds unchanging integrity, hung up his cart and announced old age for more than twenty years; his vast resolve grows firmer as he ages.

units.zh: 可謂國之碩老，邦之宗模。
units.en: He may truly be called a venerable pillar of the state and a model for the realm.
units.literal: He may be called the state's venerable elder and the dynasty's model.

units.zh: 臣聞老者不以筋力為禮，寔年逾九十，命在日制，遂自扶輿，冒險而至，展哀山陵，致敬闕庭，大臣之節備矣。
units.en: I have heard that the aged are not judged by physical strength in matters of ritual. Shi is past ninety and his days are numbered, yet he supported himself into his carriage, braved the dangers of the road, mourned at the imperial tombs, and paid homage at court—the full conduct of a great minister.
units.literal: Your servant has heard that the aged are not measured by sinew and strength in ritual; Shi is past ninety, his life measured in days, yet he supported himself into his carriage, came through danger, displayed mourning at the mausoleum, and paid respect at the palace court—the full measure of a great minister's conduct.

units.zh: 聖詔殷勤，必使寔正位上臺，光飪鼎實，斷章敦喻，經涉二年。
units.en: Imperial rescripts urged him earnestly, insisting that Shi take his proper seat at the highest level of government to bring glory to the state and sustain its substance; edict after edict pressed him for two years.
units.literal: The sacred edict was earnest, insisting that Shi take his proper place on the high terrace, illumine the tripod and nourish its substance; section upon section of rescripts urged him, spanning two years.

units.zh: 而寔頻上露板，辭旨懇誠。
units.en: Yet Shi repeatedly submitted open memorials, and the sincerity of his refusal was unmistakable.
units.literal: Yet Shi repeatedly submitted open memorials; the purport of his refusal was earnest and sincere.

units.zh: 臣以為古之養老，以不事為優，不以吏之為重，謂宜聽寔所守。」
units.en: I believe that in antiquity, honoring the aged meant freedom from office rather than weight of rank; Your Majesty should grant what Shi steadfastly requests."
units.literal: Your servant believes that in antiquity nurturing the old prized freedom from office rather than exalting official rank; it is fitting to grant what Shi steadfastly holds to."

units.zh: 三年，詔曰：「昔虞任五臣，致垂拱之化，漢相蕭何，興寧一之譽，故能光隆於當時，垂裕於百代。
units.en: In the third year an edict declared, "Ancient Shun ruled through five ministers and achieved the government of folded hands; Han's chancellor Xiao He brought an age of unity and calm—thus they shone in their own day and left an example for a hundred generations.
units.literal: In the third year an edict said, "Formerly Yu employed five ministers, achieving the transformation of folded hands; Han's chancellor Xiao He raised the praise of peaceful unity; therefore they were able to shine in their time and leave abundance for a hundred generations.

units.zh: 朕紹天明命，臨御萬邦，所以崇顯政道者，亦賴之於元臣庶尹，畢力股肱，以副至望。
units.en: I have received Heaven's mandate to rule the myriad regions; to exalt the way of government I depend on great ministers and heads of office who give their full strength as my arms and legs, answering my deepest hopes.
units.literal: I continue Heaven's bright mandate, face and govern the myriad regions; the means by which to exalt and display the way of government, also rely on these chief ministers and many directors, exhausting strength in arms and thighs, to match utmost expectation.

units.zh: 而君年耆告老，確然難違。
units.en: Yet you, venerable in years, have asked to retire, and your resolve cannot lightly be set aside.
units.literal: Yet you, lord, in years old announce old age; firmly it is hard to go against.

units.zh: 今聽君以侯就第，位居三司之上，秩祿准舊，賜几杖不朝及宅一區。
units.en: I grant you, lord, to retire to your mansion as a marquis with standing above the Three Dukes, stipend as before, the gift of a folding-stool and staff exempting you from court, and one residence.
units.literal: Now I listen to you, lord, as marquis to go to mansion; position placed above the Three Dukes; rank and emolument accord with the old; bestow folding-stool and staff, not attending court, and one mansion plot.

units.zh: 國之大政，將就諮於君，副朕意焉。」
units.en: On weighty affairs of state I shall still seek your counsel, that you may answer my deepest purpose."
units.literal: The state's great policies will go to consult with you, lord, matching my intent."

units.zh: 歲余薨，時年九十一，諡曰元。
units.en: A little over a year later he died, aged ninety-one, with the posthumous name Yuan, "Primal."
units.literal: After a little more than a year he died; at the time his years were ninety-one; his posthumous name was Yuan.

units.zh: 寔少貧窶，杖策徒行，每所憩止，不累主人，薪水之事，皆自營給。
units.en: In youth Shi was destitute; leaning on a staff he went on foot, and wherever he lodged he imposed no burden on his host, gathering his own firewood and water.
units.literal: Shi in youth was poor and mean; staff and plan, walking on foot; each place he rested, he did not burden the host; firewood and water matters, all he himself supplied.

units.zh: 及位望通顯，每崇儉素，不尚華麗。
units.en: Even when rank and fame were at their height he clung to plain frugality and scorned display.
units.literal: When position and repute were thorough and eminent, he always honored frugality and plainness, did not esteem splendor and beauty.

units.zh: 嘗詣石崇家，如廁，見有絳紋帳，裀褥甚麗，兩婢持香囊。
units.en: Once at Shi Chong's house he stepped into what he thought was a lavatory and found crimson brocade curtains, sumptuous mats, and two maids bearing sachets of incense.
units.literal: Once he went to Shi Chong's house, entered the privy, and saw there were crimson-patterned curtains, cushions and bedding very beautiful, two maids holding incense pouches.

units.zh: 寔便退，笑謂崇曰：「誤入卿內。」
units.en: Shi drew back at once and said with a smile, "I have blundered into your private rooms."
units.literal: Shi then withdrew, laughed and said to Chong, "I mistakenly entered your inner chambers."

units.zh: 崇曰：「是廁耳。」
units.en: Chong replied, "That is the privy."
units.literal: Chong said, "It is the privy only."

units.zh: 寔曰：「貧士未嘗得此。」
units.en: Shi said, "A poor scholar like me has never seen such a privy."
units.literal: Shi said, "A poor scholar has never obtained this."

units.zh: 乃更如他廁。
units.en: He asked directions to an ordinary latrine instead.
units.literal: Then he again went to another privy.

units.zh: 雖處榮寵，居無第宅，所得俸祿，贍恤親故。
units.en: Though he stood high in favor, he owned no grand mansion and spent his salary supporting kinsmen and old friends.
units.literal: Although dwelling in glory and favor, he had no mansion house; what stipend he obtained, he relieved and aided kin and old friends.

units.zh: 雖禮教陵遲，而行己以正。
units.en: Even as public morals slackened, he kept his own conduct upright.
units.literal: Although ritual teaching declined and lagged, in conducting himself he used the straight.

units.zh: 喪妻為廬杖之制，終喪不禦內。
units.en: When his wife died he observed the mourning hut and staff rites and took no concubine until the mourning ended.
units.literal: On losing his wife he made the hut-and-staff system; to the end of mourning he did not take the inner chambers.

units.zh: 輕薄者笑之，寔不以介意。
units.en: Wits mocked him for it, but he paid them no heed.
units.literal: Frivolous men laughed at him; Shi did not on that account take it to mind.

units.zh: 自少及老，篤學不倦，雖居職務，卷弗離手。
units.en: From youth to old age he studied tirelessly; even in office he never laid down his books.
units.literal: From youth to old age he loved learning without weariness; although occupying official duties, scrolls did not leave his hand.

units.zh: 尤精《三傳》，辨正《公羊》，以為衛輒不應辭以王父命，祭仲失為臣之節，舉此二端以明臣子之體，遂行於世。
units.en: He mastered the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn and corrected the Gongyang tradition, arguing that Prince Kuaire of Wei should not have refused the throne citing his grandfather's order and that Zhai Zhong had failed a minister's duty; by these two cases he defined the proper relation of subject to ruler, and his reading won wide acceptance.
units.literal: He was especially refined in the Three Traditions, discriminating and correcting the Gongyang, holding that Wei Kuaire ought not to have declined citing grandfather's command, that Zhai Zhong lost a minister's integrity; raising these two ends to clarify minister-and-son's substance, it then was practiced in the age.

units.zh: 又撰《春秋條例》二十卷。
units.en: He also compiled twenty fascicles of Spring and Autumn precedents and principles.
units.literal: Again he composed Spring and Autumn Regulations and Cases in twenty scrolls.

units.zh: 有二子，躋、夏。
units.en: He had two sons, Ji and Xia.
units.literal: He had two sons, Ji and Xia.

units.zh: 躋字景雲，官至散騎常侍。
units.en: Ji, courtesy name Jingyun, rose to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Ji, courtesy name Jingyun, office reached Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 夏以貪污棄放於世。
units.en: Xia was cast out of public life for corruption.
units.literal: Xia because of corruption was cast aside in the world.

units.zh: 弟智，字子房，貞素有兄風。
units.en: His younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Zifang, was as upright and spare in habit as his brother.
units.literal: Younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Zifang, chaste and plain had the elder brother's style.

units.zh: 少貧窶，每負薪自給，讀誦不輟，竟以儒行稱。
units.en: He grew up in want, often carried firewood to live, and never stopped his studies; in the end he won fame as a Confucian gentleman.
units.literal: In youth poor and mean, he often carried firewood to supply himself, reading and chanting without ceasing; in the end by Confucian conduct he was praised.

units.zh: 曆中書黃門吏部郎，出為潁川太守。
units.en: He served as gentleman at the palace secretariat, at the yellow gates, and in the personnel ministry, then became governor of Yingchuan.
units.literal: He successively served as gentleman of the Palace Writers, of the Yellow Gates, and of the Personnel Ministry, then went out as governor of Yingchuan.

units.zh: 平原管輅嘗謂人曰：「吾與劉潁川兄弟語，使人神思清發，昏不假寐。
units.en: Guan Lu of Pingyuan once remarked, "Conversation with Governor Liu of Yingchuan and his brothers clears the mind so that even at dusk I need no nap.
units.literal: Guan Lu of Pingyuan once said to someone, "When I with Liu of Yingchuan and his brothers speak, it causes people's spirit-thought to clear and rise; in dusk I need not borrow sleep.

units.zh: 自此之外，殆白日欲寢矣。」
units.en: With anyone else I could fall asleep in broad daylight."
units.literal: Outside of this, probably in broad daylight I wish to sleep."

units.zh: 入為秘書監，領南陽王師，加散騎常侍，遷侍中、尚書、太常。
units.en: He was recalled as director of the palace library and tutor to the prince of Nanyang, with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, then rose to palace attendant, minister of the secretariat, and minister of ceremonies.
units.literal: He entered as Director of the Palace Library, concurrently tutor to the Prince of Nanyang, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, transferred Palace Attendant, Minister of the Secretariat, Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 著《喪服釋疑論》，多所辨明。
units.en: He wrote the Discourse Resolving Doubts on Mourning Garments, which settled many disputed points.
units.literal: He composed Discourse Explaining Doubts on Mourning Dress, much was discriminated and clarified.

units.zh: 太康末卒，諡曰成。
units.en: He died toward the end of the Taikang era with the posthumous name Cheng, "Accomplished."
units.literal: He died at the end of Taikang; his posthumous name was Cheng.

units.zh: 高光，字宣茂，陳留圉城人，魏太尉柔之子也。
units.en: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a native of Yucheng in Chenliu, the son of Grand Commandant Gao Rou of Wei.
units.literal: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a man of Yucheng in Chenliu, son of Wei Grand Commandant Rou.

units.zh: 光少習家業，明練刑理。
units.en: From youth he trained in his family's legal tradition and became expert in penal law.
units.literal: Guang in youth practiced the family occupation, was clear and practiced in punishments and principles.

units.zh: 初以太子舍人累遷尚書郎，出為幽州刺史、潁州太守。
units.en: He began as household gentleman to the heir apparent and rose to gentleman of the masters of writing, then became inspector of You province and governor of Yingzhou commandery.
units.literal: At first as householder to the heir apparent by accumulated transfers became Secretariat gentleman, went out as Inspector of You Province, governor of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 是時武帝置黃沙獄，以典詔囚。
units.en: At that time Emperor Wu founded the Yellow Sand prison for prisoners sentenced by imperial edict.
units.literal: At this time Emperor Wu established Yellow Sand prison, to manage edict prisoners.

units.zh: 以光曆世明法，用為黃沙御史，秩與中丞同，遷廷尉。
units.en: Because his family had long mastered the code, Guang was named censor of Yellow Sand with rank equal to the palace assistant secretary, then promoted director of justice.
units.literal: Because Guang through generations understood law, he was used as Yellow Sand censor; rank was the same as the palace assistant secretary; he was promoted Director of Justice.

units.zh: 元康中，拜尚書，典三公曹。
units.en: During Yuankang he was appointed minister of the masters of writing in charge of the Three Dukes section.
units.literal: In Yuankang he was appointed Minister of the Secretariat, in charge of the Three Dukes bureau.

units.zh: 時趙王倫篡逆，光於其際，守道全貞。
units.en: When Sima Lun, prince of Zhao, usurped the throne, Guang held to principle and kept his integrity intact.
units.literal: When Prince of Zhao Lun usurped and rebelled, Guang at that juncture kept the Way and preserved integrity.

units.zh: 及倫賜死，齊王冏輔政，復以光為廷尉，遷尚書，加奉車都尉。
units.en: After Lun was forced to take his life and Prince Jiong of Qi directed the government, Guang was again named director of justice, then minister of the masters of writing with the added title colonel who conducts the carriage.
units.literal: When Lun was ordered to die, Prince of Qi Jiong assisted governance; again they made Guang Director of Justice, promoted Minister of the Secretariat, added Colonel Who Conducts the Carriage.

units.zh: 後從駕討成都王穎有勳，封延陵縣公，邑千八百戶。
units.en: Later he accompanied the imperial train against Prince Ying of Chengdu and earned distinction; he was enfeoffed as duke of Yanling county with one thousand eight hundred households.
units.literal: Later following the carriage in punishing Prince of Chengdu Ying he had merit; he was enfeoffed duke of Yanling county, fief one thousand eight hundred households.

units.zh: 于時朝廷咸推光明于用法，故頻典理官。
units.en: The whole court acknowledged his clarity in applying the law, so he was repeatedly placed over the judiciary.
units.literal: At that time the court all pushed Guang as clear in applying law; therefore repeatedly he managed judicial offices.

units.zh: 惠帝為張方所逼，幸長安，朝臣奔散，莫有從者，光獨侍帝而西。
units.en: When Emperor Hui was driven by Zhang Fang to take refuge in Chang'an and the court fled in panic with none willing to follow, Guang alone accompanied the emperor westward.
units.literal: Emperor Hui was pressed by Zhang Fang, traveled to Chang'an; court ministers ran and scattered; none had followers; Guang alone attended the emperor going west.

units.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍。
units.en: He was promoted left vice-director of the masters of writing with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: He was promoted Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 光兄誕為上官巳等所用，曆徐、雍二州刺史。
units.en: Guang's elder brother Dan was employed by Shangguan Si and his faction and served as inspector of Xu and Yong provinces in turn.
units.literal: Guang's elder brother Dan was used by Shangguan Si and others, successively was Inspector of Xu and Yong provinces.

units.zh: 誕性任放無倫次，而決烈過人，與光異操。
units.en: Dan was wild and unmethodical, yet bolder than most—a temper quite unlike his brother's.
units.literal: Dan's nature was unbridled and unrestrained without order, yet decisive and fierce surpassing others; with Guang his conduct differed.

units.zh: 常謂光小節，恆輕侮之，光事誕愈謹。
units.en: He constantly mocked Guang for fussiness and treated him with contempt, yet Guang served his elder brother with growing deference.
units.literal: He always called Guang petty scruples, constantly treated him lightly and insulted him; Guang serving Dan became more careful.

units.zh: 帝既還洛陽，時太弟新立，重選傅訓，以光為少傅，加光祿大夫，常侍如故。
units.en: After the emperor returned to Luoyang, the imperial younger brother had just been installed as heir and tutors were chosen with care; Guang was named junior tutor with the added title grand master of splendid carriage while keeping his post as attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: When the emperor had returned to Luoyang, at the time the imperial younger brother was newly established; heavily selecting tutors and instruction, they made Guang Junior Tutor, added Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, attendant-in-ordinary as before.

units.zh: 及懷帝即位，加光祿大夫金章紫綬，與傅祗並見推崇。
units.en: When Emperor Huai came to the throne, Guang received the grand master of splendid carriage's gold seal and purple ribbon and was honored together with Fu Zhi.
units.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended, he added Grand Master of Splendid Carriage gold seal purple ribbon, together with Fu Zhi both were seen honored and promoted.

units.zh: 尋為尚書令，本官如故。
units.en: Soon he was named director of the masters of writing while retaining his other titles.
units.literal: Shortly he became Director of the Masters of Writing; original offices as before.

units.zh: 以疾卒，贈司空、侍中。
units.en: He died of illness and was posthumously named minister of works and palace attendant.
units.literal: Because of illness he died; posthumously Minister of Works, Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 屬京洛傾覆，竟未加諡。
units.en: The fall of Luoyang followed so closely that no posthumous title was ever conferred.
units.literal: It fell when capital and Luoyang overturned; in the end no posthumous name was added.

units.zh: 子韜字子遠，放佚無檢。
units.en: His son Tao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was dissolute and unrestrained.
units.literal: His son Tao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was dissolute and unrestrained without restraint.

units.zh: 光為廷尉時，韜受貨賕，有司奏案之，而光不知。
units.en: While Guang served as director of justice, Tao took bribes; the authorities impeached him, yet Guang knew nothing of it.
units.literal: When Guang was Director of Justice, Tao received goods and bribes; the responsible office memorialized to investigate him, yet Guang did not know.

units.zh: 時人雖非光不能防閑其子，以其用心有素，不以為累。
units.en: Contemporaries faulted him for failing to restrain his son, yet because his own integrity was long established they did not let the scandal touch his reputation.
units.literal: Men of the time although blamed Guang for not being able to guard and restrain his son, because his using heart had long been plain, they did not regard it as a burden.

units.zh: 初，光詣長安留台，以韜兼右衛將軍。
units.en: Earlier, when Guang went to the provisional administration at Chang'an, he had Tao act concurrently as general of the right guard.
units.literal: Earlier, when Guang went to Chang'an's remaining terrace, he made Tao concurrently General of the Right Guard.

units.zh: 韜與殿省小人交通，及光卒，仍於喪中往來不絕。
units.en: Tao had dealings with low palace clerks, and after Guang's death he kept up those visits even during mourning.
units.literal: Tao trafficked with petty men of the palace halls and secretariat; when Guang died, still in mourning he went and came without cease.

units.zh: 時東海王越輔政，不朝觀。
units.en: Prince Yue of the Eastern Sea then directed the government and no longer attended court.
units.literal: At the time Prince of the Eastern Sea Yue assisted governance, did not attend court audience.

units.zh: 韜知人心有望，密與太傅參軍薑賾、京兆杜概等謀討越，事泄伏誅。
units.en: Tao sensed growing resentment against Yue and secretly plotted with the grand tutor's aide Jiang Ze, Du Gai of Jingzhao, and others to strike at him; the plot leaked and Tao was put to death.
units.literal: Tao knew men's hearts had expectation; secretly with Grand Tutor aide Jiang Ze, Jingzhao Du Gai, and others plotted to punish Yue; the affair leaked and he was executed.

units.zh: 史臣曰：下士競而文，中庸靜而質，不若進不足而退有餘也。
units.en: The historians write: Petty men strive for outward polish and the middling keep a dull quiet—both fall short of advancing with restraint and withdrawing while still leaving something in hand.
units.literal: The historian says: Lower gentlemen strive and are ornate; the middle way is quiet and plain; not as good as advancing insufficient yet retreating having surplus.

units.zh: 魏舒、劉寔發慮精華，結綬登槐，覽止成務。
units.en: Wei Shu and Liu Shi brought the finest of their judgment to bear, took high office beneath the court locusts, and saw their policies through to completion.
units.literal: Wei Shu and Liu Shi emitted thought's essence, tied ribbons and ascended the locust, viewed stop and completed tasks.

units.zh: 季和切問近對，當官正色。
units.en: Li Xi of courtesy Jihe answered sharp questions with plain good sense and kept a straight face in office.
units.literal: Jihe cut questions and near answers; holding office with correct color.

units.zh: 詩云「貪人敗類」，豈劉夏之謂歟！
units.en: The Classic of Poetry says, "Greedy men destroy their kin"—can that mean anyone but Liu Xia!
units.literal: The Odes says, 'Greedy men ruin the kind' — how could it mean Liu Xia!

units.zh: 贊曰：舒言不矜，憙對千乘。
units.en: Encomium: Shu spoke without swagger; Xi faced princes of a thousand chariots undaunted.
units.literal: The encomium says: Shu's words were not boastful; Xi faced a thousand chariots.

units.zh: 子真、宣茂，雅志難陵。
units.en: Zizhen and Xuanmao—noble purpose none could overthrow.
units.literal: Zizhen, Xuanmao — lofty aims hard to violate.

units.zh: 進忠能舉，退讓攸興。
units.en: They pressed loyalty and lifted the worthy; in yielding office they set a lasting example.
units.literal: Advancing loyalty, able to raise; withdrawing yielding, thereby rising.

units.zh: 皎皎瑚器，來光玉繩。
units.en: Bright as ritual coral, they brought luster to the constellations of state.
units.literal: Bright bright coral vessel; coming light to jade cord.
